findings.summary: Public command sessions are raw upstream sessions and can become orphaned/stale; command_control poll is semantically miswired.

LocalBridge CommandControlAction::Poll routes to private read_output, but running-session polling in the pinned runtime uses write_stdin with session_id and empty chars; read_output requires output_ref.

findings.summary: Silent nonzero command exits are normalized as public success instead of an explicit failed process/task outcome.
evidence: Live no-output probe cmd /c exit 7 returned coding-tools ok=true, status=exited, exit_code=7, empty stdout/stderr.

LocalBridge private_call treats this as success and normalize_command_success always emits structuredContent.ok=true/isError=false; CurrentTask therefore does not project Failed, despite stable FacadeErrorCode::ProcessFailed existing.

findings.summary: privileged-external-runtime review enforcement is bypassable because classification is lexical command-text matching.
evidence: contains_privileged_external_runtime only matches literal docker/docker.exe/podman/podman.exe/wsl/wsl.exe tokens.

findings.summary: The generation-9 shell-indirection correction remains bypassable through PowerShell .NET process-launch APIs, so privileged-external-runtime review is not fail-closed.
evidence: powershell_invocation_requires_review ignores contents inside single/double quoted strings and escalates only specific lexical words, a single call operator &, dot-source, or cmd-style expansion.

review_word includes Start-Process/CreateProcess/Win32_Process and explicit docker/podman/wsl tokens but does not include System.Diagnostics.Process, Diagnostics.Process, Process.Start, ProcessStartInfo, Shell.Application/ShellExecute, reflection type resolution, or equivalent .NET process-launch surfaces.

A command shaped as $x='<runtime executable path>'; $p=[System.Diagnostics.Process]::Start($x,'ps'); $p.WaitForExit() therefore contains no reviewed executable token outside quotes and no blocked call-operator/Start-Process token, while the shell API still chooses the process target at runtime.

A non-destructive environment probe confirmed System.Diagnostics.Process exposes 6 Start overloads on this Windows host; actual process spawning was deliberately not executed during read-only adversarial review.

Existing LB-007 regression tests cover dynamic &: $x=('do'+'cker'); & $x, Start-Process, Set-Alias, a secondary cmd, and cmd variable expansion, but do not cover .NET/COM/WMI/reflection process-launch surfaces.
runtime-policy.toml requires privileged_external_runtime=review_required, shell_invocation_review=static_target_fail_closed, and unreviewable_shell_indirection=review_required.

findings.summary: PowerShell expandable double-quoted strings hide executable $() subexpressions from the generation10 fail-closed process-target review.
evidence: powershell_member_invocation_requires_review replaces every character inside Quote::Double with spaces, so static/member launch analysis never sees an expression embedded in a double-quoted string.

powershell_invocation_requires_review likewise skips every character while Quote::Double is active, so its lexical &, Start-Process, docker/podman/wsl and indirection checks also never inspect the embedded expression.
Non-destructive Windows PowerShell probe: $v="prefix $(1+1) suffix"; Write-Output $v produced prefix 2 suffix, proving $() is executed inside expandable double-quoted strings.

Therefore a shape such as $x='<runtime path>'; Write-Output "$([System.Diagnostics.Process]::Start($x,'ps'))" can hide the generation10-blocked .NET process-launch surface inside executable interpolation while the current classifier treats the quoted region as inert data.
Current LB-007 regression tests cover direct .NET Process.Start, reflection, COM, WMI and ordinary quoted metacharacters but contain no expandable-string $() adversarial case.
runtime-policy.toml requires shell_invocation_review=static_target_fail_closed and unreviewable_shell_indirection=review_required.

findings.summary: PowerShell Alias-provider mutation remains a dynamic execution bypass around the fail-closed privileged-external-runtime review.
evidence: review_word explicitly covers set-alias/new-alias but does not cover set-item/new-item Alias-provider mutation.

Non-destructive Windows PowerShell probe: Set-Item Alias:lbgen12 Write-Output; lbgen12 'ALIAS_PROVIDER_EXECUTED' produced ALIAS_PROVIDER_EXECUTED, proving an alias can be created dynamically and then invoked as an ordinary command name.

The hook can select a CommandInfo at runtime before the later unknown command token is resolved, so protected target identity need not appear in that invocation.

findings.summary: PowerShell can create command definitions or extract and execute ScriptBlock objects without using the dynamic invocation surfaces currently classified for review.
evidence: Non-destructive Windows PowerShell probe `filter lbgen14 { Write-Output 'FILTER_DEFINITION_EXECUTED' }; lbgen14` exited 0 and produced FILTER_DEFINITION_EXECUTED; `filter` is a function-like command-definition keyword but is not classified like `function`.

Windows PowerShell probe `workflow lbgen14workflow { Write-Output 'WORKFLOW_DEFINITION_EXECUTED' }; lbgen14workflow` exited 0 and produced WORKFLOW_DEFINITION_EXECUTED; `workflow` likewise defines an invokable command.

A temporary harmless .ps1 was created outside the repository; the separate invocation `$p='<temp>\lb-gen14-probe.ps1'; $sb=(Get-Command $p).ScriptBlock; 1 | ForEach-Object -Process $sb` exited 0 and produced GEN14_SCRIPTBLOCK_FILE_EXECUTED, then the temp file was deleted. The .ps1 path remained quoted data, no call operator or Invoke method was used.

Current member scanner allows property reads such as `.ScriptBlock`; current review_word does not classify filter/workflow. This lets executable code cross the static review boundary as data and execute later.
runtime-policy.toml requires static_target_fail_closed and unreviewable_shell_indirection=review_required.

findings.summary: PowerShell member-call review remains bypassable because it denies only an enumerated set of dangerous member names.
evidence: Non-destructive Windows PowerShell probe `$ExecutionContext.InvokeCommand.InvokeScript('Write-Output GEN15_INVOKESCRIPT_EXECUTED')` exited 0 and produced GEN15_INVOKESCRIPT_EXECUTED.

findings.summary: Retained/paginated PowerShell stderr can leak private CLIXML protocol framing through the public output API.
evidence: User black-box evidence observed retained stderr containing #< CLIXML and <Objs ...>, with truncated public output ending in a mid-envelope fragment such as MS></Obj></Objs>.
src-tauri/src/mcp/facade.rs normalize_read_output copies private read_output content directly into the public result and does not invoke filter_private_stderr/public_command_stderr.

The live-session filter only enters CLIXML buffering when a chunk begins with #< CLIXML or a prior protocol buffer already exists, so retained reads beginning at a nonzero offset inside an envelope are not classifiable by that path either.
Fresh existing CLIXML unit tests pass 2/2, demonstrating a coverage gap: they test start-aware live fragmentation, not retained stderr pagination/truncation.

findings.summary: CurrentTask tracks the tools/call request lifetime instead of the full asynchronous public command-session lifecycle.
evidence: src-tauri/src/mcp/facade.rs call_tool projects Running before dispatch but unconditionally projects Idle immediately after dispatch returns.

exec_command with yield_time_ms=0 can return a stable public status=running/session_id while the underlying process continues for many seconds; call_tool nevertheless transitions CurrentTask to Idle at that response boundary.

src-tauri/src/mcp/server.rs presentation logic then retains the completed tool only for the minimum roughly 500ms visibility window, explaining the observed long-running commands whose green status indicator only flashes briefly.

Existing long-call CurrentTask tests cover a tools/call that itself remains blocked until completion/cancellation; the schema28 asynchronous session E2E exercises yield_time_ms=0 but does not assert CurrentTask remains active until that public session becomes terminal.
